quotes.text: Gen AI is really clever, but it's also quite clumsy in the sense of, you wouldn't trust it to really come up with your numbers that you need to be reliable every month and grounded in your business processes.
quotes.speaker: Rishi Sapra
quotes.why: Explains why deterministic data and logic must ground generative AI in finance.

quotes.text: Once you start with the decisions you need to make and the business questions that you need answered, then you go from there into logic and into data and then you pass that to Gen AI

takeaways: Before adding AI agents to financial data, document the business context: personas, decisions and the questions they need answered.
Certified semantic models provide deterministic KPI logic, while ontologies, skills, tools and governance add the context agents need to explain why.
As agents become more capable, governance has to be automated into the context layer and managed through a hub-and-spoke operating model with a center of excellence.
hook: Finance teams have ERP data, Power BI reports, Excel everywhere and now AI agents, yet agents do not automatically understand what revenue or margin means in their business. This conversation with Rishi Sapra is for data, BI and finance leaders who want reliable AI answers. It explains how semantic models, ontologies, skills and automated governance in Microsoft Fabric and Copilot Studio ground agents in business context.
